system:
# Context
EventStoryLine (ESL) v0.9 is an English news corpus annotated for event causality.
Documents are newswire articles grouped into topics (real-world event clusters).
Event mentions are marked inline as <ID text> (e.g. <14 checks into>, <5 conviction>).
Use the numeric ID from each tag as the mention identifier in your output.
Causal annotation covers both intra- and inter-sentence pairs; relations were annotated
wherever the link was judged direct and clear. [Reference: Caselli & Vossen, ACL 2017.]

PREDICT BOTH INTRA- AND INTER-SENTENCE RELATIONS: consider pairs of event mentions that
occur within the SAME sentence AND pairs whose mentions occur in DIFFERENT sentences —
both are in scope.

EVENTS, NOT MENTIONS: an article usually refers to the same event several times ("the
cyclone" ... "Hellen" ... "the storm"). Those mentions are one event. Before deciding
anything, group the mentions that refer to the same event.
- Never output a pair whose two mentions belong to the same group: a restatement of an
  event, or a part of it under another name, is not caused by it.
- Causality holds between EVENTS. Once you decide event X causes event Y, that link holds
  for every mention of X paired with every mention of Y, wherever they sit in the article.
  Output all of those pairs, not just the one sentence where you noticed the link.

## Label Set (Use these exact strings)
- **"causes"**: Ti causes/enables/leads to or prevents the absence of Tj (Ti → Tj).
- **"causedby"**: Tj causes/enables/leads to or prevents the absence of Ti (Tj → Ti).
- **"norel"**: No justified causal link (reject temporal-only, correlation-only, or vague plausibility).


If there are no mentions in the text and no pairs to classify, return an empty array [].

IMPORTANT:
No matter what, reason first, then output the final JSON.
user_template:
IMPORTANT:
No matter what, go through Steps 1 to 3, then output the final JSON.

Rules:
- Labels: "causes" | "causedby" | "norel".
- Consider explicit AND implicit causality; include enablement and prevention as causal.
- Mention IDs come from the <ID text> tags in the text (e.g. <14 checks into> → ID is "14").
- Consider pairs of mentions that occur within the SAME sentence AND pairs whose two
  mentions are in DIFFERENT sentences — both are in scope.
- Group mentions of the same event first. Never link two mentions of one event to each
  other. When event X causes event Y, emit the pair for EVERY mention of X against EVERY
  mention of Y, across the whole text.
- One event following another in time, or being described in the same passage, is not
  causation. Ask whether Y would still have happened as described had X not happened.
- Return a JSON array of causal pairs (omit a pair to mark it norel):
[
  {{"pair":"14,44","label":"causes"}},
  {{"pair":"44,14","label":"causedby"}}
]

Coherence Rules:
- Symmetry: "A,B" "causes" implies "B,A" "causedby" and inversely — both must appear.
- Omission: Any pair you leave out is treated as norel.
- Contradiction: "A,B" "norel" is incompatible with "A,B" "causes" or "A,B" "causedby".

Text:
{doc_text}

IMPORTANT:
No matter what, reason first, then output the final JSON.
